title: Senpai is an Otokonoko
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Makoto Hanaoka dresses as a girl at school but hides it from his mother, who wants a 'manly' son. Saki Aoi, a bisexual first-year, falls for Makoto and keeps loving him after learning he is a boy, while his childhood friend Ryuji realizes he also has feelings for him, forming a love triangle (Wikipedia; Webtoon text via AniList; ANN).
life_message: Love and friendship should accept people as they are, and being honest about oneself takes courage worth supporting.

content.note: Love triangle with same-sex and bisexual feelings (Wikipedia; AniList); nothing explicit noted (MU Wholesome).
Loneliness, pressure at home and judgment at school (Wikipedia; ANN); bullying (MU; AniList spoiler).

dominant: gender expression and self-acceptance; love regardless of gender; family disapproval

frames.aligns: Respect for persons; Makoto's loneliness met with friendship.
frames.concerns: Gender expression and same-sex love affirmed against Church teaching.

frames.aligns: Compassion for a lonely young man.
frames.concerns: Crossdressing and same-sex romance shown as good.
Gender and sexuality message conflicts with BF&M; mother cast as obstacle.

frames.aligns: Opens talk about loneliness and honesty with parents.
frames.concerns: Affirming message on gender and sexuality.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Worth held regardless of others' judgment (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Makoto dresses as he chooses despite school and home norms (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friends accept him more than family (Wikipedia).

folkways.japan: The otokonoko subculture and senpai-kohai school relationships shape the setting, and pressure to conform at school reflects Japanese group-harmony norms, described here as context.

delivery.evidence: ANN calls it subtle and open to interpretation; Wikipedia notes author's intended theme and a stated line in chapter 31.
delivery.note: The disapproving mother is given a family backstory, though the story clearly sides with Makoto.

winners_losers: Makoto, Saki and Ryuji grow through honesty and acceptance; the mother's insistence on manliness is shown as harmful but rooted in her own past. Sympathy lies with self-acceptance.
